summary: Completed comprehensive frontend testing of new Supabase auth feature addition. All auth pages (signup, login), form validations, navigation links, protected routes, and CSS styling work correctly.
passed_tests: Landing page at / loads correctly with all elements
Signup page renders at /signup with all 4 fields (Full Name, Email, Password, Confirm Password)
Signup form validation: empty fields show errors
Signup form validation: password min 8 chars shows error
Signup form validation: password mismatch shows error
Signup password toggle visibility works
Signup confirm password toggle visibility works
Signup 'Back to Home' link navigates to /
Signup 'Already have an account? Log in' link navigates to /login
Login page renders at /login with Email and Password fields
Login form validation: empty fields show errors
Login password toggle visibility works
Login 'Forgot Password?' link shows 'Password reset is coming soon!' toast
Login 'Back to Home' link navigates to /
Login 'Don't have an account? Sign up' link navigates to /signup
Protected route /courses redirects to /login when not authenticated
Protected route /dashboard redirects to /login when not authenticated
Admin dashboard at /referral still works correctly (not protected)
CSS brand variables applied (--bg-primary: #02073D, --color-primary: #246BFD, etc.)
Glassmorphism card styling on auth pages (backdrop-filter: blur(20px), rgba background, border)
test_credentials: No test credentials needed - UI-only testing without actual Supabase auth
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth feature addition complete. Supabase client configured in src/lib/supabase.js. AuthContext provides signUp/signIn/signOut. Protected routes use ProtectedRoute component. All form validations are client-side. HTML5 email validation works as first layer, custom regex validation as second layer. Toaster uses sonner library directly (not Shadcn wrapper).
notes: Email format validation uses both HTML5 native validation (type='email') and custom regex validation. The HTML5 validation triggers first for obviously invalid emails. Custom validation catches edge cases that pass HTML5 but fail the regex pattern.
